audio.title: Riser covers the payoff words 'whole new human' in the consonant band
audio.evidence: riser.wav (vol 0.6, starts at 25.433 s) stays within 1 dB of its peak from 1.0 to 2.0 s into the file, which is 26.43-27.43 s in the film. That is exactly the words 'whole' 26.26, 'new' 26.65, 'human' 26.92-27.37. In the 1-4 kHz band (consonants), voice minus riser is -10.6 dB on 'whole', -12.3 dB on 'new' and -7.7 dB on 'human'. Full band: 'new' +0.6 dB, 'human' -0.5 dB. Momentary loudness: the riser is 0.7-8.4 LU louder than the voice from 27.0 to 27.5 s. 94% of the riser's energy is above 1 kHz (bands 1-4k -5.8 dB, >4k -6.3 dB).
audio.fix: In src/audio/clips.ts and Soundtrack.tsx, let Clip.volume also be a function of the frame (Remotion's <Audio volume={f=>...}>). Duck the riser to about 0.08 (-18 dB) from 26.2 to 27.4 s and ramp it back to 0.6 by 27.6 s, so it swells into the 27.4-27.9 s gap before 'Hello, world'. Simpler alternative: drop the riser to 0.15 or below for its whole length.
audio.betterFix:
Keep the riser on the flash and just turn it down. In src/audio/clips.ts, change the riser's volume from 0.6 to about 0.18-0.2 (roughly -10 dB). The voice then sits about 10-12 dB above it overall and level-to-+5 dB in the 1-4 kHz band on 'whole new human'. The swell still peaks on the 26.67 s flash.

If more riser is wanted around the words, widen Clip.volume to number | ((f: number) => number). Soundtrack.tsx already passes c.volume straight to <Audio volume>, so only the type changes. Then give the riser a curve in clip-local frames, counted from its start at 25.433 s, with clamped extrapolation:

interpolate(f, [0, 22, 25, 58, 62], [0.6, 0.6, 0.2, 0.2, 0.45])

That is full level up to 'whole' (26.17 s), down to 0.2 under the words through 27.37 s, then back to 0.45 for the flashOut and the tail. Don't drop it to 0.08 across the flash.

audio.title: Kick thump is almost all sub-bass: barely there on phones, but on full-range speakers it is louder than the voice and is the film's loudest peak
audio.evidence: kick.wav band shares: 51% below 80 Hz (-2.9 dB), 80-200 Hz -15.5 dB, 200-1k -28.2 dB, 1-4k -35.1 dB. This comes from sfx.py: a sine falling from 80 Hz to 38 Hz plus noise through a one-pole low-pass (coefficient 0.02, about 150 Hz cutoff). A 200 Hz high-pass (phone model) removes 22.9 dB of it, leaving it 8.3 dB under the voice on a phone. Full band, its loudest 50 ms is +12.6 dB above the median voice, and voice minus kick is -3.4 dB on 'first' and -1.8 dB on 'kick.'. It is the film's highest sample, -1.41 dBFS at 21.976 s. Because of it, the final loudness pass turns the whole mix down by about 0.8 dB from 21.75 to 22.25 s (final-vs-raw gain 1.83 dB there, 2.62-2.66 dB around it), which also lowers the words. The tail is cut off: the last sample is 0.0112 (-39 dBFS) at 22.567 s, right before 1 s of digital silence.
audio.fix: In scripts/audio/sfx.py kick_thump: start the pitch sweep higher (for example f = 60 + 120*exp(-t/0.04)) and add a 2nd harmonic or a short 300-800 Hz 'knock' at about -12 dB. Raise the low-pass coefficient from 0.02 to about 0.08, high-pass at 40 Hz, and add a 30 ms fade-out. Then in clips.ts lower the kick from 0.9 to about 0.4, so its full-band level sits about 6 dB under the voice but it can still be heard above 200 Hz.
audio.betterFix:
In scripts/audio/sfx.py kick_thump, keep the sub but add a much louder mid layer. Either add a 400-600 Hz knock at about -6 to -3 dB relative to the sine, decaying over about 20 ms, or add a 2nd harmonic of about 0.25 and gently saturate the sine. Start the sweep near 160-180 Hz and fall to about 55 Hz. Raise the noise low-pass coefficient to about 0.08, high-pass at 35-40 Hz, and fade out over the last 30 ms.

In src/audio/clips.ts, set the kick volume to about 0.5 (not 0.4). In my test with the -3 dB knock at 0.5:
- Through a 200 Hz high-pass, the kick's loudest 50 ms is about 1 dB under the median voice.
- Through 400 Hz, it is about 3 dB under.
- K-weighted, it is about +1 dB, and that peak falls in the pause between "first" and "kick.".
- The raw-mix peak drops to about -3.9 dBFS, below the 0.62 s peak, so the loudness-pass dip at 22.0 s goes away.

Keep the kick starting at 21.967 s, in that pause. After the change, re-render and re-check the kick level through 200 and 400 Hz high-pass filters and K-weighted.

audio.title: Fertilisation impact starts with a hard click, and its boom is lost on phones
audio.evidence: The first sample of impact.wav is -0.512 and the next samples stay near -0.55 to -0.6, so the take starts mid-waveform with no fade-in. In the film this is a one-sample jump of -10.5 dBFS at 4.967 s (the biggest edge discontinuity in the mix), and 3 kHz+ energy jumps 9.3 dB above the ongoing voice. 66% of the impact's energy is below 80 Hz (-1.8 dB share), and the 200 Hz+ share is about -24 dB. On phones the impact is -10.4 dB under the voice (18.2 dB lost to the high-pass), so mostly the click survives. Full band it is +5.9 dB above the median voice and equal to the voice on 'wins.' (-0.4 dB). Clarity is fine: speech band +20.6 dB.
audio.fix: In scripts/audio/sfx.py, pass af_extra='highpass=f=35,afade=t=in:d=0.004,equalizer=f=250:t=q:w=1:g=5' to normalize_peak for the impact. This gives a de-clicked onset and more mids that phones can play. Then lower the impact in clips.ts from 0.75 to about 0.5.
audio.betterFix: Keep the de-click part. In scripts/audio/sfx.py, pass af_extra='highpass=f=35,afade=t=in:d=0.004' for the impact. Keep the fade after any filter, so the filter cannot ring on the step at sample 0. You can drop the 250 Hz EQ: it only adds about 5 dB to the phone band and the boom stays inaudible there. Volume 0.5 in clips.ts is fine (about -0.8 dB full-band against now, because the peak normalisation makes up the loss). To make the impact audible on phones, the sound needs real content between 120 and 400 Hz. Either layer a short body thump under it, for example a variant of kick_thump() with its pitch falling from about 220 Hz to 90 Hz over 0.1 s, mixed about 12 dB under the impact and with its own 4 ms fade-in. Or switch to another ElevenLabs impact take that has more mid content. Check the result with a 200-250 Hz high-pass model: the boom after the click should be within about 10 dB of the voice.

audio.title: Cell pops have a doubled attack, and each one starts with a step click
audio.evidence: pop.wav envelope at 1 ms resolution: a first transient at 3-6 ms (-4 dB re peak), a dip of about -20 to -27 dB from 13-27 ms, then the main hit at 32-42 ms (0 dB). That is two onsets about 36 ms apart, heard as 't-pop' rather than one clean pop. The pitched copies keep it: pop-hi about 28 ms, pop-hi2 about 22 ms, pop-lo about 51 ms (close to two separate hits). The body after the main hit (~50 ms, then -24 dB by 90 ms) does sound like a pop. All four files start at a non-zero sample (0.052-0.057, about -25 dBFS) with no fade-in (sfx.py: atrim=0.05:0.40, no afade in). In the film: pop at 7.633 s is a -33 dBFS step (3k+ energy +32 dB over the moment before), pop-hi at 8.367 s is -34 dBFS (+58 dB over the silence before), pop-lo at 10.600 s steps out of exact digital zero. Levels themselves are fine: speech band +6.5 dB on 'two', +6.6 dB on 'hundreds'.
audio.fix: In scripts/audio/sfx.py build(), trim the pop take just before the main transient and add a fade-in: normalize_peak(..., -4, 'atrim=0.078:0.43,afade=t=in:d=0.002,afade=t=out:st=0.28:d=0.07'). The main onset is at about 0.082 s in the source. Then regenerate pop-hi, pop-hi2 and pop-lo.
audio.betterFix:
In scripts/audio/sfx.py build(), add asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS right after the atrim, so the fade times count from the start of the trimmed clip:
normalize_peak(src(root, "pop"), f"{d}/pop.wav", -4, "atrim=0.078:0.43,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,afade=t=in:d=0.003,afade=t=out:st=0.27:d=0.08")

I checked this version: the first samples are 0.000, there is a single onset, and the tail fades smoothly to 0.35 s.

Then run build() again. It regenerates pop-hi, pop-hi2 and pop-lo from pop.wav automatically. If the pop body should stay on the onset of 'two' and 'four', change their clip offsets in src/audio/clips.ts from -0.02 to about +0.01. Apply the same asetpts fix to any other atrim+afade chain.

audio.title: Smaller clicks: first whoosh, first heartbeat, kick tail
audio.evidence: whoosh.wav and whoosh-low.wav start at -0.0186 (-34.6 dBFS). At 0.467 s this is a -42 dBFS step out of digital silence, with 3k+ energy +47 dB over the silence before (a faint tick before the first word). heartbeat.wav starts at -0.0325 (-29.8 dBFS) because the first lub's grain is placed at t0 = 0.0436 s*SR - peak_off(0.08 s), which is negative, so its first 36 ms are dropped. The comment says 'pad front', but the code writes [0.0]*0. It is hidden under 'heart' at 13.4 s. The kick ends abruptly at 22.567 s (see the kick finding).
audio.fix: sfx.py: add afade=t=in:d=0.01 to the whoosh normalize_peak call. In heartbeat_track, pad the front with peak_off samples (out = [0.0]*int(0.08*SR) + out, and shift t0 by the same amount), then move the heartbeat in clips.ts earlier by 0.08 s (beat('Scene3','heartStarts',-0.08)) so the lub stays in sync.
audio.betterFix:
Whoosh: keep the proposed fix, normalize_peak(src(root,"whoosh"), f"{d}/whoosh.wav", -3, "afade=t=in:d=0.01"). whoosh-low inherits it.
Heartbeat, zero-risk option (it is masked under the VO anyway): after placement, fade in the first 5 ms of `out`, `for j in range(int(0.005*SR)): out[j] *= j/(0.005*SR)`. Fix the 'pad front' comment. No timing change is needed.
Heartbeat, full-attack option: use a pad of whole frames, `pad = int(0.1*SR)` (3 frames). Allocate `out = [0.0]*(int((HEART_LEN+0.3)*SR) + pad)`, place with `j = t0 + pad + i`, and use `fade0 = pad + int((HEART_LEN-HEART_FADE)*SR)`. Do NOT also prepend zeros at write time. In clips.ts, use beat('Scene3','heartStarts',-0.1). sec() then gives exactly frame 399, so the lub peak stays at 13.4436 s, the same as now. Update the comment to say the track's t=0 is 3 frames before heartStarts.
Kick: as in the kick finding, fade the last ~30 ms of kick_thump to zero, or lengthen the tail until it decays below -60 dBFS.

audio.title: Two stretches of exact digital silence across scene cuts
audio.evidence: silencedetect at -50 dB on the final film: 22.585-23.592 s (1.007 s), which spans the Scene4->5 cut at 23.0 s; the kick tail is cut off just before it. Also 10.964-11.597 s (0.633 s), which spans the Scene2->3 cut at 11.0 s; samples there are exactly zero (pop-lo decays to zero by 11.02 s, and l4 starts at 11.5 s). Nothing in the mix bridges either cut. The music you are adding later may fill them; this only matters if the music is quiet or ducked at those points.
audio.fix: When music is added, make sure it plays through 10.9-11.6 s and 22.5-23.6 s. Otherwise give the kick and pop-lo a short decaying tail (for example aecho=0.6:0.5:60|120:0.3|0.15 in sfx.py), or add a soft low whoosh at about vol 0.25 starting at 22.85 s and 10.85 s in clips.ts.
audio.betterFix:
Leave this until the music is in, then run silencedetect again (-50 dB, d=0.3). Only the kick change below is worth doing whatever the music does.
1) Kick (scripts/audio/sfx.py, kick_thump): change n = int(0.6 * SR) to n = int(1.0 * SR). The exp(-t/0.14) envelope then fades to about -60 dB on its own, instead of stopping at about -39 dBFS at 0.6 s. That removes the hard stop and carries the tail to about 22.97 s, right up to the 23.0 s cut. To keep the length at 0.6 s instead, multiply the last 40 ms by a linear ramp to zero.
2) Only if the gaps are still exposed after the music: add a quiet bridge tied to the scene starts, not fixed seconds. In src/audio/clips.ts, import FPS (already imported) and SCENE_START and add:
{ src: "sfx/whoosh-low.wav", at: SCENE_START.Scene3 / FPS - 0.15, volume: 0.2 },
{ src: "sfx/whoosh-low.wav", at: SCENE_START.Scene5 / FPS - 0.15, volume: 0.2 },
Then listen to check it doesn't mask the first word of l4 ("Week six") or l7 ("Week forty"). Do not use aecho.

audio.title: Heartbeat is louder than 'a tiny heart starts to beat'
audio.evidence: heartbeat.wav (vol 0.85) starts at 13.4 s while line l4 is still being spoken (until 14.75 s). Its loudest 50 ms is +8.0 dB above the median voice level, in both full band and above 200 Hz. Voice minus heartbeat, full band: 'heart' +2.8, 'starts' -2.2, 'beat.' -5.5 dB. In 200 Hz-1 kHz, where the doppler thump sits (59% of its energy is in that band): 'starts' -9.1, 'beat.' -7.7 dB. Momentary loudness: voice minus heartbeat swings between -4.8 and +6.7 LU from 13.5 to 14.8 s.
audio.fix: Using the same frame-based volume in clips.ts and Soundtrack.tsx, hold the heartbeat at about 0.2 (-12.5 dB) from 13.4 to 14.75 s, then ramp to 0.85 by 14.9 s. The heart then sits under the voice and comes up on its own from 14.8 to 16.6 s. Picture sync at 13.4 s is unchanged.

overlays.title: Two captions are drawn on top of each other at 2.33-2.63s and 20.17-20.47s
overlays.evidence: In out/qa-viewer-overlap.png: at 2.40s and 2.50s, 'Millions' sits right on top of 'It starts with a race.' At 20.30s and 20.40s, the new line's 'Week' is stacked over the fading 'Week twelve: fingers, toes, a face.', which looks like doubled text. Cause in src/overlays/Captions.tsx: a line fades out from end+6 to end+16 frames, but the next line's first word starts appearing 2 frames before its start time. The gaps are too short for that: l1 ends 2.102 and l2 starts 2.40 (0.30s apart); l5 ends 19.935 and l6 starts 20.25 (0.32s apart). Both lines use the same position (CAPTION_Y 1420).
overlays.fix: In src/overlays/Captions.tsx (LineView), end each line's fade before the next line starts: pass the next line's start time in and use fadeEnd = Math.min(sec(end)+16, sec(nextStart)-2) and fadeStart = fadeEnd-6. Also make the filter that keeps a line on screen (frame <= sec(l.end)+18) stop at that same fadeEnd.
overlays.betterFix: In Captions.tsx, give each line the start frame of the next line's first word: next = LINES[i+1] and nextAt = next ? sec(next.words?.[0] ?? next.start) : Infinity. In LineView, set fadeEnd = Math.min(sec(line.end)+16, nextAt-2) and fadeStart = Math.min(sec(line.end)+6, fadeEnd-6), so lines with no clash keep their current end+6 to end+16 fade. Use fadeStart and fadeEnd for both the `out` and `lift` tweens. fadeEnd-fadeStart is always at least 6, so interpolate's input range stays strictly increasing. Results: l1 fades over frames 64-70 and l2 starts at 70; l5 fades over frames 600-606 and l6 starts at 606. All other lines stay as they are. In the filter, changing frame <= sec(l.end)+18 to frame <= fadeEnd is optional, since opacity is already 0 after fadeEnd.

overlays.title: The ending is flat: 'Hello, world.' looks like any other subtitle and is gone before the last frame
overlays.evidence: From 28.0 to 29.0s, 'Hello, world.' uses the same 76px bottom caption style as every other line. It fades out from 29.13 to 29.47s (l8 ends 28.933, plus 6 to 16 frames). The final frame (out/qa-viewer/x_last.png, frame 899) has no title, no week tracker and no text at all: just the hand gripping the finger in the top half, the adult finger cut off at the right edge, and the bottom 45% of the frame filled by a dark sleeve. Motion nearly stops after 28.5s (frame change 1.7-4.0). The thumbnail and the payoff moment carry no message.
overlays.fix: In src/overlays/Captions.tsx, give l8 a 'final' treatment: no fade-out (hold to frame 899), a bigger size (about 120-140px) and a position in the empty lower half (about y 1250-1350), so it reads as the closing title. In src/scenes/Scene5/grip, keep a slow push-in running through the last 1.5s and frame the grip a little lower and more centred.
overlays.betterFix: In src/overlays/Captions.tsx, treat the last line (l8) as the end title. For l8 only, skip the out/lift tweens and widen the filter so it stays on screen through frame 899 (TOTAL_FRAMES - 1). Set its size to about 104-116px so it stays on one line, and optionally make "world" gold. Keep it at CAPTION_Y (1420) or move it slightly lower (about 1460-1500), never above about 1400, because the pink cuff fills y 1030-1355 there. To keep the hold from feeling static, add a very slow scale or letter-spacing settle on l8 over its last 1s. Leave the Scene5 grip framing as it is. The push-in already runs to T.last; at most, soften its easing so it doesn't settle so early. Don't move the grip lower, because that pushes the cuff into the caption zone.

overlays.title: Science mismatches in the day/week tracker and the 'first kick' line
overlays.evidence: The DAY counter runs ahead of the cells: DAY 04 shows 2 cells (8.0s), DAY 05 shows 4 cells (8.5s), DAY 06 shows the morula (9.5s). In reality: 2 cells around day 1-2, 4 cells around day 2, morula around day 3-4, blastocyst at day 5. The tracker then jumps DAY 06 > WEEK 01 > WEEK 03 > WEEK 06 between 10.75 and 11.25s while the blastocyst is still implanting. Week 3 is roughly right for implantation, but the label flashes by and switches from days to weeks mid-scene, which reads as an error. Also, 'Week twenty: the first kick' (20.25-22.5s) is not accurate: the fetus moves from about 8 weeks, and 18-20 weeks is when the mother first feels it (scene4 brief, Accuracy).
overlays.fix: In the WeekTracker overlay or the timing map, tie DAY labels to the visible stage: zygote D1, 2 cells D2, 4 cells D2-3, morula D4, blastocyst D5, implantation D6-7. Hold DAY 07 through implantation, then switch to weeks as the Scene3 crossfade starts. For the kick, consider changing the script.ts text and VO to something like 'Week twenty: a kick you can feel.' (this needs a new VO take, which also needs a working ElevenLabs key).
overlays.betterFix: Fix only the KEYS array in src/overlays/WeekTracker.tsx. Change the values only, nothing else. Replace the single [5.0, 1/7] to [10.6, 6/7] segment with points tied to the beats, in global seconds. The label rounds w*7, so plan for that rounding. [5.0, 1/7] gives D1 at the zygote. [7.65, 2/7] gives D2 at 'two'. [8.4, 3/7] gives D3 at 'four'. [9.3, 4/7] gives D4 at the morula. About [10.0, 5/7] gives D5 at the blastocyst/hatching. [10.6, 6/7] gives D6 at implant contact. Then hold [10.95, 7/7 minus a tiny amount] so the label stays at DAY 07; use something like 0.99 so the label does not flip to 'WEEK 01' early. Then [11.4, 6] makes it roll to WEEK 06 during the Scene3 crossfade (11.0-11.5s), before the 'Week six' VO at 11.6s. That keeps the roll-up look but starts it once the implantation visuals hand off. Leave the 'first kick' VO as it is. A caption-only change would no longer match the spoken line, and a new take needs a valid ElevenLabs key: the one the user gave returns 401 Invalid API key. If the user still wants it changed later, re-record l6 with a new key and update script.ts and voTiming.ts together.

overlays.title: Week counter still uses the old 20.4s 'week twenty' time, so it counts up to 20 while the week-12 face is still lit
overlays.evidence: src/overlays/WeekTracker.tsx:12 hard-codes [19.8, 12], [20.4, 20], which matched the old weekTwenty beat of 20.4s and is not read from BEATS. After the retime the face highlight runs to local 125 (20.17s). Scene1.title: Weak hook: the first second is almost still, and the only motion is in the bottom 25% of the frame
Scene1.evidence: Average frame-to-frame change is only 1.1-1.3 out of 255 from 0.00 to 0.50s and 1.3-2.0 from 0.50 to 1.50s (most of the film is far higher). At 0.0s and 0.5s the frame is a still egg on a dark background; 0.5s adds only the word 'It'. The sperm first appear around 1.0s as thin, faint lines at y>1440. Measured motion there is 3-4 versus about 1 in the rest of the frame. That bottom strip is where TikTok and Reels put their own text and buttons. The swarm reaches the middle of the frame only around 2.0s. Someone scrolling sees a still image for the first second.
Scene1.fix: In src/scenes/Scene1 and src/theme/beats.ts, move Scene1.raceStart to about 0.1-0.2s and have the front of the swarm already in the middle of the frame (y 900-1300) on frame 0, with near-layer sperm crossing toward the egg. Or open with a slow camera push or a light flicker on the egg so frame 0 already has motion. Keep frame 0 good-looking as the thumbnail.
Scene1.betterFix:
Keep frame 0 as the clean egg thumbnail and add motion from the first frames:

1. In beats.ts, set Scene1.raceStart to about local("Scene1", 0.15), which is 4-5 frames. It must stay above 0 for the camera keys in camera.ts. The whoosh SFX moves with it to about 0.03s, so the opening is no longer silent.
2. In swarmSpecs.ts, lower the spawn bands so the leading sperm are already crossing the bottom edge on frame 0. The far layer spawns at screen y 1950+ and the near layer at 2000+; change both to about 1750-2100. Keep the mid finalists close to their current spawn so their arrival timing holds.
3. Route 1-2 near-layer sperm (big and sharp) on a diagonal that crosses above y 1300, outside the caption band, within the first 0.5s. That puts motion in the upper frame, clear of the TikTok/Reels UI strip.
4. In camera.ts, make the slow push start at frame 0 and actually show. Today zoomK only goes from 1.0 to 1.004 by raceStart; make it about 1.0 to 1.03, or let the egg's breath and corona shimmer start at frame 0.
5. Re-render and check:
   - The winner still touches the zona at oneWins and the flash still lands at fertilise.
   - No spec hits the speed clamp in finish().
   - Frame 0 still reads as a clean thumbnail.
   - The upper 75% of the frame shows motion of about 0.8 or more within the first 0.5s.

Scene2.title: Scene2: the 2-to-4 split now starts while the two cells are still at their biggest springy bounce, and the two-cell pause is half as long
Scene2.evidence: The gap between 'two' and 'four' shrank from 30 to 22 frames. src/scenes/Scene2/timeline.ts:27 still ends the 1-to-2 split at local 47, and timeline.ts:28 (B.four-17) now starts the next split at local 55-57. That is only 8 frames after the cells are born. The old timing gave 16 frames (42 to 58). At 8 frames HERO_SPRING (cells.ts:24, cells.ts:69) is at 1.25, its peak overshoot (I computed this with remotion spring). In the old timing it had settled to 0.96. The furrow at cells.ts:59 lerps from that still-moving position. The new nuclei (cells.ts:73, brk+2 to brk+10, so 49 to 57) never reach full strength before they dissolve again from local ~56. Film frames 224-241 (out/qa-retime-s2-two.png) show nuclei only faintly from local 50-56, then the spindle and furrow take over. So the 'hero' two-cell state is on screen for about 0.23s. The four-cell state (out/qa-retime-s2-four.png, 73-78) is now held longer than it.
Scene2.fix: In src/scenes/Scene2/timeline.ts:28 change GENS[1] to { start: B.four - 13, dur: 10, jitter: 2 }. I simulated this in a scratch copy (out/qa-retime-lin-fix.cjs). The 2-to-4 split then starts at local 59-61 (12 frames of rest, spring at about 0.93) and still completes at 69-71, right on 'four' (72) and its pop sound effect.

Scene2.title: Scene2: the 'hundreds' cascade is no longer tied to the word. The morula forms 6 frames late, and the staggered cell flow into the blastocyst is lost
Scene2.evidence: Several timings now collide. timeline.ts:32 (32-to-64 split starts at B.hundreds-9 = 90) is now earlier than timeline.ts:31 (16-to-32 starts at B.four+19 = 91). That window is never used: the clamp at lineage.ts:104 pushes it to 99-100. The 64-cell morula therefore forms at local 104-105, 5-6 frames after 'hundreds' (99, VO word at 9.313s). In the old timing it formed at 107-108, on the word (108). CAV.start = B.hundreds+1 = 100 (timeline.ts:40) and cavityOpen starting at B.hundreds (timeline.ts:41) now come before the morula exists. The clamp at prims.ts:62 (max(CAV.start+delay, birth+1)) overrides the stagger delay on all 64 of 64 cells. In the old timing it overrode 0 of 64. The ring and ICM delays from blasto.ts:101/106 are wiped out: every cell starts flowing at 105-106 in lockstep, where before the starts were spread over 109-114. The morula never rests (1 frame). Scene5.title: Caption becomes hard to read during the birth flash (about 25.6-26.7s)
Scene5.evidence: I measured the background behind the captions (y 1300-1560) with out/qa-viewer-lum.py. Most of the film gives white text a contrast of 15-18:1. At 26.0s it drops to about 2.9:1, at 26.2s to 2.2-3.6:1, at 26.4s to 2.1-2.8:1 and at 26.6s to 2.8-3.1:1. Those are the frames where 'a whole new' appears (word times 26.10, 26.26, 26.65). In out/qa-viewer-flash.png, white text sits on a pale pink and gold wash, and at 25.6-26.0s the gold crack lines and the light column run straight through 'cell has become'. This breaks the Scene5 brief rule 'Never leave the caption zone bright', and it happens on the film's key line.
Scene5.fix: In src/scenes/Scene5/womb (the light-bloom and wall-opening layer), add a dark scrim for the caption zone (y 1250-1600, wombDeep at about 0.6 alpha, feathered edges) between BEATS.Scene5.birth-10 and human+10 frames. Or start the light bloom below y 1650 and limit its brightness. Keep the crack lines from crossing y 1300-1560.
Scene5.betterFix: Fix the timing of the existing CaptionScrim instead of adding a new layer. In src/scenes/Scene5/index.tsx, tie the scrim to the moment the bloom switches on, not to `bright`. Use for example `const scrim = tween(frame, T.bloom - 4, T.bloom + 12, [0, 0.85], EASE.out) * (1 - 0.25 * flash);`. This keeps it at about 0.65-0.85 through 25.6-26.9s and keeps the multiply blend, so there is no dark band. Before the bloom the zone is already dark, so starting earlier is not needed. Optionally, also stop the Bloom from aiming straight at the caption. In womb/BirthLight.tsx, move SRC.y from 1760 to about 1900, or push the white `C.text 0%` stop of its radial gradient further out. You could also raise the Flash's rose/womb floor stops a few percent (e.g. rose at 58%, womb at 66%) so all of y 1300-1560 is covered at the peak. Re-render, then re-measure 25.6-26.8s with out/qa-refuteflash-lum.py. Target: the background median should stay at 4.5:1 or better.
